title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 10 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Science Classification' broadly test?
options: Whether a group of items share a common scientific category (from physics, chemistry, biology, etc.)
questions.rationale: Science classification tests whether items share a common scientific category, drawing on knowledge across scientific disciplines.

questions.question: What does 'Chemistry Classification' test specifically?
options: Whether a group of substances/elements share a common chemistry-based category (element type, compound class, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether substances or elements share a common chemistry-related category, such as being the same type of element or compound.

questions.question: What does 'Biology Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of organisms/biological items share a common biological category
questions.rationale: This tests whether organisms or biological items share a common biological classification, such as taxonomic group or biological function.

questions.question: What does 'Human Body Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of body parts/systems share a common anatomical or functional category
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of body parts or systems share a common anatomical or functional category, identifying the one that belongs elsewhere.

questions.question: What does 'Computer Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of computing-related items share a common technical category (hardware, software, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether computing-related items share a common technical category, such as all being hardware components or all being software types.

questions.question: What does 'Programming Classification' test, specifically?
options: Whether a group of programming-related terms share a common category (languages, paradigms, concepts, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether programming-related terms share a common category, such as all being programming languages or all being coding concepts.

questions.question: What does 'File-Type Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of file extensions/types share a common category (document, image, executable, etc.)
questions.rationale: This tests whether file types share a common category, such as all being image formats or all being document formats.

questions.question: What does 'Operating System Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of items relate to a common category of operating systems or their components
questions.rationale: This tests whether items share a common category related to operating systems, identifying the one that belongs to a different category.

questions.question: What is the 'Tool vs Product Classification' distinction?
options: That tools and products are always the same thing
Distinguishing whether an item functions as a tool (used to make something) versus being the resulting product itself
That only products can be classified
That only tools can be classified
questions.rationale: This distinguishes items that function as tools (used to create or work on something) from items that are themselves the finished product — a subtle but important distinction.

questions.question: What is the 'Function-Based Trap'?
options: Mistakenly classifying by superficial category when the true shared property is actually about function or use
A trap only relevant to numbers
A trap with no practical relevance
questions.rationale: This trap involves classifying based on a superficial category resemblance, when the true shared property that matters is actually about function or use.
